notebook:
T34, 49/50 solves. Best valid = 0.000 (empty design), so final score = 0.000 unless a nonempty design is valid AND positive. Gambling one solve is free (a negative valid design is still worse than empty? No — score = best valid design evaluated; empty scores 0, so any negative design doesn't beat 0.000; a positive one does).
Learned: columns cost ~$110-190M/yr at high reflux/stages, so any revenue must exceed that. Revenue needs a stream >=95% pure (or blend). Easiest gaps: C4/C5 (~28K) and C5/C6 (~14K), not nC6/MCP (~3K).
Single-column cannot make a C4 mix top cut because C3 (propylene+propane 286 mol/s) rides along (~63% C4 only). A side draw in the rectifying section could theoretically concentrate C4 between C3 overhead and C5 bottoms. C4 mix (iC4+nC4=544 mol/s) at 85% of mean price (~0.0119) = ~$186M/yr, near the column cost, so break-even at best.
LAST MOVE: feed col 90 st, reflux 6, boil-up 6, dp 0.3, liquid side draw stage 30 frac 0.20 (avoid stage 45 = feed stage). See if S is >=95% C4 mix or T/B anything sellable. If it converges non-positive, final = 0.000 (empty).
